title: Trump gets another shot in his quest to overturn hush money conviction | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

President Donald Trump has been given another chance to try to move the appeal of hisconvictionon state charges tied to hush money payments before a federal court — a move that could speed up the decision over whether the verdict is overturned.

On Monday, the 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals said Trump can try again to persuade a district court judge that his appeal on 34 state counts of falsifying business records should be heard by federal judges.

The president has argued his appeal should be heard by federal judges because it involves questions involving federal election law and the Supreme Court’s presidential immunity decision, which came down weeks after his conviction.

Trump wasconvicted in 2024 on 34 state counts of falsifying business recordsto reimburse hush money payments made to silence adult film star Stormy Daniels before the 2016 presidential election.

Judge Alvin Hellerstein had rejected Trump’s argument to move the case into federal court three times. Hellerstein passed away last month. The case has not yet been assigned to another judge.

Whoever is assigned the case will put fresh eyes on the legal questions that began in 2023 and escalated after Trump was convicted in May 2024 and the Supreme Court issued its decision on presidential immunity two months later.

If the new district court judge decides the case should be moved to federal court, then the Second Circuit would likely evaluate the case on the merits. Any further appeals would go to the Supreme Court, allowing it to interpret its own ruling on immunity. It would also fast track the decision to the Supreme Court, which otherwise would not hear the case until all appeals at the state court levels are exhausted, which could take years.

Earlier this month, Trump’s lawyer argued before a state appellate court panel that they should overturn the verdict. That court has not yet ruled, and the three-judge panel that ruled Monday said those proceedings should pause in the meantime.

A spokesman for Trump’s legal team celebrated the decision. “President Trump appreciates the Second Circuit’s prompt and correct ruling, as he continues to win against Democrat weaponization of our Justice System. As today’s order highlights, the Supreme Court’s historic decision on Immunity, the Federal Constitution, and other established legal precedent mandate that the Witch Hunt perpetrated by the Manhattan DA be removed to federal court, and immediately overturned and dismissed. President Trump will keep defeating the Liberal Hoaxes at every turn.”

A spokesperson for the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office declined to comment.

In Monday’s decision, the panel of judges, two nominated by Democrats and one nominated by a Republican, said Hellerstein erred by ruling that removal is not allowed after a federal officer defendant is convicted and by finding that Trump’s lawyers failed to show “good cause” or a good reason for him to ask the judge to reconsider.

Trump’s lawyers had argued they had good cause because they didn’t know how much the district attorney’s office would rely on federal election law in the trial and the Supreme Court decision, which limited evidence of official conduct from being used against the president in a case about unofficial conduct.

At the hearing last week Steven Wu, chief of appeals for the DA’s office, argued the case is not about tweets or Trump’s conversations with Hope Hicks, the White House communications adviser who testified at trial.

“The defendant is not being prosecuted here for publishing his tweets. He’s not being prosecuted for speaking with Ms. Hicks in the White House.” The case, he said, is about falsifying business records to commit or conceal another crime, which could have been violating state or federal election law, tax laws or falsifying bank business records.

This story has been updated with additional details.
